residency.test: Based on where your personal and economic life is centred - home, family, work, registration and bank accounts - rather than a day count.
residency.worldwide_income: Yes for residents, with treaty relief.
residency.note: Income is split into three boxes taxed under different rules: box 1 work and home, box 2 substantial shareholdings, box 3 savings and investments.

headline.note: the first two rates include national insurance contributions of 27.65%
headline.credits: general tax credit up to 3,068 and labour credit up to 5,599, both income-tested
headline.expat_regime: the 30% ruling gives qualifying incoming employees a tax-free allowance, capped at the WNT norm

income_tax.name: Box 1 income tax and national insurance
income_tax.note: rates for taxpayers below state pension age; the first bracket is 17.92% tax plus 27.65% national insurance

credits.name: Arbeidskorting (labour credit)
credits.note: builds up across three phases at low incomes; this models the plateau and phase-out

employer.name: WW Awf and sector funds
employer.note: higher rate applies to flexible contracts

capital_gains.box3: savings and investments are taxed on a deemed return applied to net assets above the 57,684 exemption, currently at 36%. The Supreme Court has forced a route to be taxed on actual return where that is lower.
capital_gains.box2: substantial shareholdings (5% or more) are taxed at 24.5% up to 67,804 and 31% above
capital_gains.shares: there is no general capital gains tax on listed shares held by individuals - box 3 taxes the holding, not the gain
capital_gains.principal_residence: gains on your own home are untaxed; mortgage interest is deductible against box 1 at a restricted rate

quirks: There is no capital gains tax on ordinary investments. Box 3 taxes an assumed return on your net wealth instead, so a bad investment year can still produce tax.

The 30% ruling for incoming employees is capped at the WNT norm and has been progressively trimmed. Check the version that applies to your start date rather than assuming the historic 30% for five years.
The general and labour credits phase out steeply, so the real marginal rate in the 43,000-76,000 range is well above the headline 37.48%.
Mortgage interest deduction (hypotheekrenteaftrek) is capped at a 37.48% benefit even for top-rate taxpayers, and is reduced by the deemed rental value of the home (eigenwoningforfait).
Fiscal partners can freely allocate certain shared items between their returns, which is a genuine planning opportunity most people miss.

reporting.who_must_file: Anyone who receives an invitation (aangiftebrief), anyone owing more than the small threshold, and anyone expecting a refund - filing voluntarily is common and often worthwhile.

deadlines.what: Extended deadline if you request an extension before 1 May
Deadline for taxpayers filing through a tax adviser under the collective arrangement
File by this date and the Belastingdienst aims to respond before 1 July

forms.name: Annual income tax return, largely pre-filled online
Migration year return, for the year you arrive in or leave the Netherlands
Provisional assessment for monthly refunds or payments

documents_to_collect: WOZ value of your home and annual mortgage statement
Bank and investment balances as at 1 January - box 3 uses that single date
Records of deductible gifts, healthcare costs and study expenses

penalties.late_filing: verzuimboete of up to 385 for a first offence, more for repeats
penalties.late_payment: interest (belastingrente) from 1 July following the tax year
penalties.incorrect_return: up to 100% of the underpaid tax where there is intent

warnings: The 30% ruling is not applied automatically. If it applies, reduce gross salary by the exempt portion before running the calculation.
The labour credit build-up phases at low incomes are simplified to a plateau and taper.
Box 3 wealth tax is not computed - it depends on asset composition on 1 January, not on income.
